description: Experience the unparalleled taste of Classic Butter Chicken, a cherished Indian delicacy. Tender chicken pieces are simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based gravy, infused with aromatic spices and a hint of butter. This Murgh Makhani recipe promises a delightful balance of sweet and savory flavors, perfect for a comforting meal.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 min

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, 1/2 tsp red chili powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric, garam masala, and 1/2 tsp salt. Mix well to coat all chicken pieces. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of unsalted butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, cooking in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes per batch, turning occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics for the Sauce
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of unsalted butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until it turns translucent and soft. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant, ensuring it does not burn.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy Base
instructions.text: Add the pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews, remaining 1/2 tsp red chili powder, remaining 1/4 tsp turmeric, and 1/2 tsp salt to the pan. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pan and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and you see oil separating from the sides, indicating the tomatoes are well cooked.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain for Smoothness
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked tomato and cashew mixture from the pan to a blender. Blend until the sauce is completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky texture, pour the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down with a spoon to extract all the liquid and leaving behind any fibrous bits.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken pieces to the smooth, strained sauce in the pan. Stir in the heavy cream, sugar, and the crushed kasoori methi. Simmer gently on low heat for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce and for the sauce to warm through. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Once the Butter Chicken is heated through and the flavors have melded beautifully, remove from heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve your Classic Butter Chicken hot with warm naan bread, steamed basmati rice, or tandoori roti for a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For best flavor, marinate the chicken for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Soaking cashews is crucial for a smooth and rich gravy. Dont skip this step.
Straining the gravy after blending ensures a restaurant-quality silky texture. Use a fine-mesh sieve.
Adjust the spice level by increasing or decreasing red chili powder according to your preference.
Serve immediately with warm naan, roti, or basmati rice. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
article:
Mastering the Art of Classic Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, known in its authentic form as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian chicken recipe is a global favorite, celebrated for its rich, creamy texture, tantalizing aroma, and perfectly balanced sweet and savory notes. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality experience in your own kitchen, you've come to the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to prepare a classic Butter Chicken that will impress even the most discerning connoisseurs.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, India, it was created by Kundan Lal Gujral. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken pieces were simmered in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream, giving birth to a legend. The dish quickly gained popularity and became a staple of North Indian cuisine.

At its core, Butter Chicken features tender pieces of chicken (traditionally tandoor-cooked, though home versions often use pan-fried or grilled chicken) bathed in a luscious, vibrant orange-red sauce. This sauce is a complex symphony of flavors, built upon a base of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a medley of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, coriander, and fenugreek (kasuri methi). The finishing touches of fresh cream and a generous knob of butter provide its signature silken texture and luxurious mouthfeel, making it an irresistible culinary delight.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

To embark on your Murgh Makhani journey, gather these essential ingredients. Quality matters, especially for the tomatoes and cream, which form the backbone of the sauce.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani (Butter) Sauce:
*   2 tbsp ghee or unsalted butter, plus extra for finishing
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 ripe medium tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, optional but recommended for extra creaminess)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1 tsp ground coriander
*   1/2 tsp ground cumin
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1-2 tsp sugar (to balance acidity)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus extra for garnish
*   Salt to taste

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Classic Butter Chicken

Creating the perfect Butter Chicken involves a few distinct stages, each contributing to the final masterpiece.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken**: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.

2.  **Cook the Chicken**: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base**: In the same pan, add another tablespoon of ghee or butter. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Build the Flavor**: Stir in the turmeric powder, red chili powder, ground coriander, and ground cumin. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until the spices are aromatic.

5.  **Add Tomatoes and Cashews**: Pour in the crushed tomatoes or fresh tomato puree. If using soaked cashews, drain them and add them to the pan. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to soften completely.

6.  **Blend the Sauce**: Carefully transfer the entire sauce mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot). Blend until perfectly smooth. For an extra silky sauce, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on any solids. This step is crucial for that restaurant-style smoothness.

7.  **Finish the Sauce**: Return the pan to medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken back into the smooth sauce. Stir in the garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, and sugar. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the sauce's flavors.

8.  **The Grand Finale**: Stir in the heavy cream and a generous knob of unsalted butter (1-2 tablespoons). Cook for another 2-3 minutes, just until the sauce is heated through and creamy, being careful not to boil after adding the cream. Taste and adjust salt and sugar as needed.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

*   **Marination is Key**: The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Don't skip this step!
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder**: For that vibrant orange-red color without excessive heat, use Kashmiri chili powder. It's milder and primarily used for its beautiful hue.
*   **Don't Rush the Sauce**: Allow the tomatoes to cook down thoroughly. This removes their raw taste and deepens the sauce's flavor.
*   **Blend and Strain**: For an authentic, velvety smooth Butter Chicken, blending the sauce until absolutely smooth and then straining it is non-negotiable. This removes any fibrous bits from onions, ginger, or tomato skin.
*   **Kasuri Methi**: This dried fenugreek leaf is a secret weapon in Murgh Makhani. Gently crush it between your palms before adding to release its unique, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor.
*   **Balance is Everything**: The sweetness from sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Adjust to your preference. A pinch of black pepper can also enhance the overall profile.
*   **Smoky Flavor (Dhungar)**: For an authentic touch, after the dish is complete, heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot. Place it in a small steel bowl in the center of the chicken. Drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over the charcoal, cover immediately for 2-3 minutes to infuse a smoky aroma. Remove charcoal before serving.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Classic Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments.

*   **Naan Bread**: Soft, fluffy naan (plain, garlic, or butter) is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce.
*   **Basmati Rice**: Steamed basmati rice, especially fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice), provides a light counterpoint to the creamy curry.
*   **Roti or Chapati**: For a healthier option, whole wheat roti or chapati also makes an excellent companion.
*   **Fresh Salad**: A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) offers a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.
*   **Garnish**: A swirl of fresh cream, a sprinkle of chopped fresh cilantro, or a slice of green chili adds visual appeal and a burst of freshness.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic recipe is divine, Murgh Makhani is also adaptable to different preferences and dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian Butter Paneer**: Substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) cubes. Marinate and pan-fry the paneer lightly before adding it to the sauce. Tofu can also be used for a vegan option.
*   **Spice Level**: Adjust the amount of red chili powder to suit your heat preference. For more heat, add green chilies along with ginger-garlic paste.
*   **Dairy-Free**: Use coconut milk or cashew cream instead of heavy cream, and a dairy-free butter substitute. Ensure your yogurt for marination is also dairy-free.
*   **Chicken Cooking Method**: If you have a grill or an air fryer, cooking the marinated chicken in either of these methods can impart a lovely char and smoky flavor, mimicking the traditional tandoor.
*   **Healthier Option**: Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or use low-fat cream. The sauce will still be delicious, just slightly less decadent.

Butter Chicken is more than just a recipe; it's an experience. With this detailed guide, you're well-equipped to create a truly unforgettable Murgh Makhani that will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of India. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and delight in the incredible flavors of this beloved Indian classic.
